title: Compact linear inverse maps and the Picard criterion

items.title: Hilbert-space Moore–Penrose inverse

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2, Theorem 3.3
Otmar Scherzer and Leonidas Mindrinos, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, University of Vienna, 2015

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $X$ and $Y$ be real or complex Hilbert
spaces over the same scalar field, and let $K:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear
operator. Write $R(K):=\{Kx:x\in X\}$ for its range,
$N(K):=\{x\in X:Kx=0\}$ for its kernel, and
$M^\perp:=\{z:\langle z,m\rangle=0\text{ for every }m\in M\}$ for the
orthogonal complement of a subspace $M$. The kernel $N(K)$ is closed, so the
restriction
$$\widetilde K:=K|_{N(K)^\perp}:N(K)^\perp\to R(K)$$
is a linear bijection. Define the Hilbert-space Moore–Penrose inverse $K^\dagger$
to have domain
$$D(K^\dagger):=R(K)\oplus R(K)^\perp$$
and, for the unique decomposition $y=r+z$ with $r\in R(K)$ and
$z\in R(K)^\perp$, set
$$K^\dagger y:=\widetilde K^{-1}r.$$
Thus $K^\dagger y$ is the unique minimum-norm solution of $Kx=r$, and the
orthogonal-range component is mapped to zero. Boundedness of $K^\dagger$ on
this domain is not part of the definition.

items.title: Compact linear inverse model between Hilbert spaces

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2, §3.1
Otmar Scherzer and Leonidas Mindrinos, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, University of Vienna, 2015

items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar field, and let
$K:X\to Y$ be a compact linear operator. The associated compact linear inverse
model has parameter space $X$, data space $Y$, forward map $K$, and admissible
truth class $X$: for a true parameter $x^\dagger\in X$, the exact datum is
$y=Kx^\dagger\in Y$. Given an exact datum $y\in Y$, solving this inverse
problem means finding a parameter $x\in X$ such that $Kx=y$. No injectivity,
surjectivity, or closed-range assumption is included in the model.

items.title: Closed range and boundedness of the Hilbert pseudoinverse

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2, Theorem 3.7
Otmar Scherzer and Leonidas Mindrinos, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, University of Vienna, 2015, Theorem 6.6 (singular-system context)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K:X\to Y$ be the compact linear
operator of a real or complex Hilbert-space inverse model, and let
$K^\dagger:D(K^\dagger)\to X$ be its Hilbert-space Moore–Penrose inverse, with
$D(K^\dagger)=R(K)\oplus R(K)^\perp$ carrying the norm inherited from $Y$.
Then $K^\dagger$ is bounded on its domain if and only if $R(K)$ is closed in
$Y$; for compact $K$, these conditions are also equivalent to $R(K)$ being
finite-dimensional. Here bounded means that some real $C\ge0$ satisfies
$\|K^\dagger y\|_X\le C\|y\|_Y$ for every $y\in D(K^\dagger)$.

items.title: Picard range and pseudoinverse-domain criterion

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2, Theorem 3.10
Otmar Scherzer and Leonidas Mindrinos, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, University of Vienna, 2015, Theorem 6.7
Vesa Kaarnioja, Inverse Problems: Fourth Lecture, FU Berlin, 8 May 2023

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K:X\to Y$ be a compact linear map
between real or complex Hilbert spaces, with Hilbert adjoint $K^*:Y\to X$.
Write $\mathbb N_{>0}:=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$. If $R(K)$ has finite dimension
$r\in\mathbb N$, put $J=\{1,\ldots,r\}$, interpreted as empty when $r=0$;
if $R(K)$ is infinite-dimensional, put $J=\mathbb N_{>0}$. Thus $J$ indexes
exactly the positive singular values $s_j>0$ in nonincreasing order. Let
$(v_j)_{j\in J}$ and $(u_j)_{j\in J}$ be complete
orthonormal families in $N(K)^\perp$ and $\overline{R(K)}$, respectively,
with $Kv_j=s_ju_j$ and $K^*u_j=s_jv_j$. The empty sum is zero, finite $J$
uses a finite sum, and infinite $J$ uses the norm-convergent series whenever
the stated square-summability condition holds. Use inner products linear in the
first argument. Define the Picard sum
$$P_K(y):=\sum_{j\in J}\frac{|\langle y,u_j\rangle_Y|^2}{s_j^2},\qquad y\in Y.$$
Then:

1. The exact equation $Kx=y$ is solvable if and only if
   $y\perp N(K^*)$ and $P_K(y)<\infty$.

2. The domain of the Hilbert-space Moore–Penrose inverse is
   $$D(K^\dagger)=R(K)\oplus R(K)^\perp=\{y\in Y:P_K(y)<\infty\},$$
   and for every $y\in D(K^\dagger)$,
   $$K^\dagger y=\sum_{j\in J}\frac{\langle y,u_j\rangle_Y}{s_j}v_j.$$
   Thus the orthogonal component in $R(K)^\perp=N(K^*)$ is discarded by
   $K^\dagger$; exact range membership additionally requires that component
   to be zero.

title: Compact linear inverse maps and the Picard criterion — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A nonzero left-null datum passes the series test but is not in the range

references.title: Otmar Scherzer and Leonidas Mindrinos, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, University of Vienna, 2015, Theorem 6.7
Vesa Kaarnioja, Inverse Problems: Fourth Lecture, FU Berlin, 8 May 2023, PDF pp. 10–12

items.statement:
With standard Euclidean inner products, take $K:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^2$ given
by $Kx=(x,0)$. Define $K^*:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ by $K^*(a,b)=a$; for
all $x\in\mathbb R$ and $z\in\mathbb R^2$ it satisfies
$\langle Kx,z\rangle=\langle x,K^*z\rangle$, the defining adjoint identity.
For this map let $R(K):=\{Kx:x\in\mathbb R\}$ and
$N(K^*):=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:K^*z=0\}$. Its sole positive singular pair is
$s_1=1$, $v_1=1$, $u_1=(1,0)$: these are unit vectors spanning the input and
range, and $Kv_1=s_1u_1$, $K^*u_1=s_1v_1$. Define the Picard sum for this
pair by
$$P_K(y):=\frac{|\langle y,u_1\rangle|^2}{s_1^2}.$$
Then $y=(0,1)$ satisfies $P_K(y)=0<\infty$ and
$y\in N(K^*)\setminus\{0\}$, but $y\notin R(K)$.

items.title: A compact diagonal map with dense nonclosed range

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2, Theorems 3.9–3.10, §§3.1–3.2
Vesa Kaarnioja, Inverse Problems: Fourth Lecture, FU Berlin, 8 May 2023, PDF pp. 10–12

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. On the real Hilbert space
$H=\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$, define the diagonal map
$(Kx)_n=x_n/(n+1)$ for $n\in\mathbb N$, where $\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$
and $e_n$ is the coordinate vector at $n$. In positive indexing, its singular
system is $s_j=1/j$ and $v_j=u_j=e_{j-1}$ for $j\ge1$. Then $K$ is compact and
its range is dense but not closed. The datum $y=(1/(n+1))_{n\in\mathbb N}$
lies in $H$ and in $\overline{R(K)}$, but not in $R(K)$; its Picard sum
$$\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\frac{|\langle y,e_{j-1}\rangle|^2}{s_j^2}$$
diverges, so the equation $Kx=y$ has no exact solution.
